OrganizationPersonalReply.description: The answer to a successful ensure: the caller's personal tenant and whether this call registered it.

created.description: Whether this call registered the tenant

OrganizationPersonalTenant.description: The personal tenant the ensure names.

alias.description: The request-surface name. It is the account's username, or the derived identifier when the account carries no username

id.description: The tenant identifier, derived deterministically from the account identifier: the fixed prefix "personal-" followed by the account identifier. The scoped tables hold it, so it takes no phone number, display name or other personal data, and it does not change with the request language

kind.description: The tenant kind; the frontend renders the personal organization label from it

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence, present only when the answering module has one to give. It may be a sentence rendered in the request language or a language-neutral token such as "forbidden", so clients must not parse it.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

post.description: Backfills the caller's personal tenant when the account's own membership is missing, and reads it back otherwise. Every call completes the tenant's tenant-admin role and the caller's binding and converges the role's grants to the module's allowlist. A membership row that exists is left as it stands, and a tenant that is not enabled is refused without a write. The tenant identifier is derived from the account identifier, and the alias is the account's username; the answer names the tenant and whether this call created it.

200.description: The personal tenant, complete; created says whether this call registered it

403.description: The caller is a service account, or a static-table subject that cannot own a tenant

409.description: The caller cannot have a personal tenant: its personal tenant exists and is not enabled (tenant-unavailable), or the derived identifier or alias is unavailable (identifier-unavailable). The type field names which. tenant-unavailable changes if an operator enables the tenant, and identifier-unavailable does not change on retry

503.description: A dependency could not answer; no part of the result is returned

post.summary: Ensure the caller's personal tenant exists and is complete
